title: Germany news: Bremerhaven port to receive defense boost
summary: Bremerhaven's port and Bremen's airport will be upgraded for German, NATO defense needs in case of an attack on the alliance. It comes as European countries upgrade militarily amid Russia's war in…
byline: Wesley Dockery, Richard Connor, Roshni Majumdar

image.caption: Bremerhaven is Germany's second-biggest cargo port after Hamburg Image: Jochen Tack/picture alliance

blocks.text: Bremerhaven's port to be upgraded for German, NATO defense needs
The North Sea port of Bremerhaven will be upgraded to better serve German and NATO defense needs, German officials said on Tuesday.

German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius signed a memorandum of understanding on Tuesday which will transform the port into a "Deployment Hub" in the case of an attack on the NATO bloc. The plan will cost some €1.5 billion ($1.7 billion).

blocks.caption: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius (right) signed the memorandum of understanding with Bremen Mayor Andreas BovenschulteImage: Sina Schuldt/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 has caused European countries to draw up plans in case of an attack on a NATO member, such as Germany.
"Tens of thousands of soldiers will need accomodation and food. Machinery and equipment must be maintained and operated accordingly," Pistorius said.

Bridges, roads and railways will need to be boosted to facilitate the transportation of NATO equipment arriving at the Bremerhaven port. Bremen's airport will also be expanded with more logistics space as part of the plan.
